Connect another database package to a user's sign-in

Source: R/session.R
oauth_db_connect.Rd

Use this when a database driver accepts an OAuth token and has no dedicated shinyOAuthDB helper. Supply the function that opens its connection and name the argument that receives the token.

Usage

oauth_db_connect(
  authorization,
  connect = DBI::dbConnect,
  ...,
  token_arg = "token",
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  disconnect = NULL,
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

connect

Function that opens the connection, such as DBI::dbConnect.

...

Named arguments for connect, excluding the token argument.

token_arg

Name of the argument that receives the user's access token.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

disconnect

Function to close the connection. By default, DBI connections use DBI::dbDisconnect(); other objects have no cleanup.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function such as con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression to get the connection. Before sign-in, it waits quietly, like shiny::req().

Details

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. The helper reuses the connection and calls its cleanup function when the selected authorization changes, ends, or loses required permissions, or when the Shiny session ends. Cleanup depends on the driver; a retained native handle may still contain copied credentials. Call con() before each operation.

A valid DBI connection stays open through token refresh. If the connection becomes invalid, the next call opens a new one.

While token refresh is running, reactive outputs wait and can resume when it finishes. A button-triggered query may need another click. min_valid_for checks token lifetime at the start of an operation; it does not guarantee validity throughout a long query.

This helper supplies the token when opening a connection. For a function that takes a token on each request, use oauth_db_token() or a platform API client.

See also

oauth_db_token(). For saved results and connection lifetime, see vignette("getting-started", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Other advanced connection helpers: oauth_db_fabric(), oauth_db_token()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Inside server(); client configured for Azure PostgreSQL:
con <- oauth_db_connect(
  auth$connection,
  connect = DBI::dbConnect,
  drv = RPostgres::Postgres(),
  token_arg = "password",
  target = "postgres",
  host = "example.postgres.database.azure.com",
  dbname = "reporting",
  user = "reporting-readers",
  sslmode = "verify-full"
)
} # }
